course_name_original: Fundamentos Químicos De La Ingeniería (I.Mecánica / I.Tecnologías Industriales / I.Energía)
course_name_en: Chemical Fundamentals of Engineering (Mechanical Eng. / Industrial Technologies Eng. / Energy Eng.)
prerequisites: Basic chemistry knowledge from previous educational stages, especially knowing how to formulate chemical compounds. Proficiency in solving problems and questions related to reaction stoichiometry, expressing solution concentrations, and pH calculations is required.

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects implying knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of industrial engineering within the scope of Energy.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: Non-metallic elements of Groups VII A and VI A
Non-metallic elements of Groups V A and IV A
Semimetallic elements of Groups IV A and III A
Metals: Metallurgical processes. Representative metals. Groups I A, II A, III A, IV A
Natural resources in the Organic Chemistry industry
teaching_methods: Continuous Assessment Tests and self-assessment exercises
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated based on two options. Option A (with Continuous Assessment Tests - PECs): Final grade = Final Exam grade (PP) + PECs grade + Laboratory Practices grade. PECs contribute a maximum of 0.5 points to the final grade (0.25 points per PEC). Laboratory Practices contribute a maximum of 0.5 points. Both PECs and Practices grades are added only if the PP grade is 4 points or higher, and Practices are passed (5 points or higher). Option B (without PECs): Final grade = Final Exam grade (PP) + Laboratory Practices grade. Practices grade is added only if the PP grade is 5 points or higher, and Practices are passed (5 points or higher). Laboratory practices are mandatory and must be passed (5 points or higher) to pass the course; failure results in a "NOT APT". If the ordinary exam is not passed, an extraordinary exam is held in September, for which PECs and Practices grades are carried over. Passed laboratory practices are valid for six years.
